'''Bai Chunli''' ({{zh |s = 白春礼}}; born September 26, 1953) is a Chinese [[physical chemist]], [[Nanotechnology|nanotechnology scientist]], and [[Academic administration|academic administrator]]. He is a professor at the Chinese Academy of Sciences Institute of Chemistry. 

In academia, Bai served as president of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] from 2011 to 2020 and as president of the [[University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences]] from 2001 to 2014. In organizations, Bai served as president of the [[The World Academy of Sciences|World Academy of Sciences]] from 2012 to 2018, as vice chairperson of the [[China Association for Science and Technology]] from 2001 to 2011, and as chairperson of the [[Chinese Chemical Society (Beijing)|Chinese Chemical Society]] from 1999 to 2010.<ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1038/news.2011.180 |title = Chinese Academy of Sciences has big plans for nation's research |journal = Nature |year = 2011 |last = Qiu |first = J. |doi-access = free }}</ref>

Bai is honorary president of the [[University of Science and Technology of China]] and of the [[University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=中国科学院大学名誉校长白春礼：储备科技创新硬核竞争力--教育--人民网 |url=http://edu.people.com.cn/n1/2019/0904/c1053-31335999.html |access-date=2022-09-17 |website=edu.people.com.cn |archive-date=20 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920171447/http://edu.people.com.cn/n1/2019/0904/c1053-31335999.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="University of Science and Technology of China" />

== Early life and education ==
Bai Chunli's father was a teacher in a public elementary school before the [[Chinese Civil War|Civil War]]. When Bai was young, his father taught and explained ancient poems and their messages to Bai.<ref>{{Cite web |title=白春礼：从战士到院士-中国科大新闻网 |url=http://news.ustc.edu.cn/info/1051/35674.htm#:~:text=%E7%88%B6%E4%BA%B2%E6%98%AF%E4%B8%AA%E5%84%92%E9%9B%85%E8%80%8C%E6%AD%A3%E7%9B%B4%E7%9A%84%E4%BA%BA%EF%BC%8C%E8%A7%A3%E6%94%BE%E5%89%8D%E6%9B%BE%E5%9C%A8%E5%85%AC%E7%AB%8B%E5%B0%8F%E5%AD%A6%E5%BD%93%E8%BF%87%E6%95%99%E5%91%98%E3%80%82%E8%B5%8B%E9%97%B2%E6%97%B6%EF%BC%8C%E4%BB%96%E5%B8%B8%E7%BF%BB%E7%9D%80%E4%B8%80%E6%9C%AC%E6%9C%AC%E6%B3%9B%E9%BB%84%E7%9A%84%E8%AF%97%E9%9B%86%EF%BC%8C%E7%BB%86%E8%87%B4%E8%80%8C%E5%8F%88%E7%94%9F%E5%8A%A8%E5%9C%B0%E4%B8%BA%E7%99%BD%E6%98%A5%E7%A4%BC%E8%AE%B2%E8%A7%A3%E8%AF%97%E4%B8%AD%E7%9A%84%E8%95%B4%E4%B9%89%E3%80%81%E8%AF%97%E4%BA%BA%E5%B4%87%E9%AB%98%E7%9A%84%E6%B0%94%E8%8A%82%E3%80%81%E8%BF%9C%E5%A4%A7%E7%9A%84%E6%8A%B1%E8%B4%9F%E3%80%82%E6%98%AF%E4%BB%A5%E7%AB%A5%E5%B9%B4%E6%97%B6%E6%9C%9F%E7%9A%84%E7%99%BD%E6%98%A5%E7%A4%BC%E6%9C%80%E7%88%B1%E8%83%8C%E5%8F%A4%E8%AF%97%E8%AF%8D%EF%BC%8C%E6%9C%80%E5%B4%87%E6%8B%9C%E8%AF%97%E4%BA%BA%EF%BC%8C%E6%9C%80%E6%83%B3%E5%BD%93%E4%BD%9C%E5%AE%B6%E3%80%82 |access-date=2022-09-17 |website=news.ustc.edu.cn |archive-date=20 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920170433/http://news.ustc.edu.cn/info/1051/35674.htm#:~:text=%E7%88%B6%E4%BA%B2%E6%98%AF%E4%B8%AA%E5%84%92%E9%9B%85%E8%80%8C%E6%AD%A3%E7%9B%B4%E7%9A%84%E4%BA%BA%EF%BC%8C%E8%A7%A3%E6%94%BE%E5%89%8D%E6%9B%BE%E5%9C%A8%E5%85%AC%E7%AB%8B%E5%B0%8F%E5%AD%A6%E5%BD%93%E8%BF%87%E6%95%99%E5%91%98%E3%80%82%E8%B5%8B%E9%97%B2%E6%97%B6%EF%BC%8C%E4%BB%96%E5%B8%B8%E7%BF%BB%E7%9D%80%E4%B8%80%E6%9C%AC%E6%9C%AC%E6%B3%9B%E9%BB%84%E7%9A%84%E8%AF%97%E9%9B%86%EF%BC%8C%E7%BB%86%E8%87%B4%E8%80%8C%E5%8F%88%E7%94%9F%E5%8A%A8%E5%9C%B0%E4%B8%BA%E7%99%BD%E6%98%A5%E7%A4%BC%E8%AE%B2%E8%A7%A3%E8%AF%97%E4%B8%AD%E7%9A%84%E8%95%B4%E4%B9%89%E3%80%81%E8%AF%97%E4%BA%BA%E5%B4%87%E9%AB%98%E7%9A%84%E6%B0%94%E8%8A%82%E3%80%81%E8%BF%9C%E5%A4%A7%E7%9A%84%E6%8A%B1%E8%B4%9F%E3%80%82%E6%98%AF%E4%BB%A5%E7%AB%A5%E5%B9%B4%E6%97%B6%E6%9C%9F%E7%9A%84%E7%99%BD%E6%98%A5%E7%A4%BC%E6%9C%80%E7%88%B1%E8%83%8C%E5%8F%A4%E8%AF%97%E8%AF%8D%EF%BC%8C%E6%9C%80%E5%B4%87%E6%8B%9C%E8%AF%97%E4%BA%BA%EF%BC%8C%E6%9C%80%E6%83%B3%E5%BD%93%E4%BD%9C%E5%AE%B6%E3%80%82 |url-status=live }}</ref> In 1966, Bai Chunli went to middle school, and after only 4 years of study, he got a high school diploma.<ref>{{Cite web |title=白春礼：从战士到院士-中国科大新闻网 |url=http://news.ustc.edu.cn/info/1051/35674.htm |access-date=2022-09-17 |website=news.ustc.edu.cn |archive-date=20 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920170433/http://news.ustc.edu.cn/info/1051/35674.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Graduating from high school during the [[Cultural Revolution]], Bai joined the [[Down to the Countryside Movement]] with other young people. He worked at the [[Inner Mongolia]] production and construction corps mechanical transport company as a driver and clerical staff from September 1970 to September 1974.<ref name="scitech.people.com.cn">{{Cite web |title=中国科学院院长白春礼--科技--人民网 |url=http://scitech.people.com.cn/n/2014/0528/c385209-25076775.html |access-date=2022-09-17 |website=scitech.people.com.cn |archive-date=20 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920171508/http://scitech.people.com.cn/n/2014/0528/c385209-25076775.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 1974, after three rounds of secret balloting for the soldiers of the whole company, and later taking written examinations, Bai Chunli became an undergraduate student of [[Peking University]] as a "[[Worker-Peasant-Soldier student|worker, peasant and soldier student]] with practical experience."<ref>{{Cite web |title=白春礼：从战士到院士-中国科大新闻网 |url=http://news.ustc.edu.cn/info/1051/35674.htm#:~:text=1974%E5%B9%B4%EF%BC%8C%E7%BB%8F%E8%BF%87%E5%85%A8%E8%BF%9E%E6%88%98%E5%A3%AB%E4%B8%89%E8%BD%AE%E4%B8%8D%E8%AE%B0%E5%90%8D%E6%8A%95%E7%A5%A8%E8%AF%84%E9%80%89%E5%92%8C%E5%8F%82%E5%8A%A0%E6%96%87%E5%8C%96%E8%80%83%E8%AF%95%EF%BC%8C%E7%99%BD%E6%98%A5%E7%A4%BC%E4%BD%9C%E4%B8%BA%E4%B8%80%E5%90%8D%E2%80%9C%E6%9C%89%E5%AE%9E%E8%B7%B5%E7%BB%8F%E9%AA%8C%E7%9A%84%E5%B7%A5%E5%86%9C%E5%85%B5%E5%AD%A6%E5%91%98%E2%80%9D%E6%88%90%E4%B8%BA%E5%8C%97%E4%BA%AC%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6%E7%9A%84%E5%AD%A6%E7%94%9F%E3%80%82 |access-date=2022-09-17 |website=news.ustc.edu.cn |archive-date=20 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920170433/http://news.ustc.edu.cn/info/1051/35674.htm#:~:text=1974%E5%B9%B4%EF%BC%8C%E7%BB%8F%E8%BF%87%E5%85%A8%E8%BF%9E%E6%88%98%E5%A3%AB%E4%B8%89%E8%BD%AE%E4%B8%8D%E8%AE%B0%E5%90%8D%E6%8A%95%E7%A5%A8%E8%AF%84%E9%80%89%E5%92%8C%E5%8F%82%E5%8A%A0%E6%96%87%E5%8C%96%E8%80%83%E8%AF%95%EF%BC%8C%E7%99%BD%E6%98%A5%E7%A4%BC%E4%BD%9C%E4%B8%BA%E4%B8%80%E5%90%8D%E2%80%9C%E6%9C%89%E5%AE%9E%E8%B7%B5%E7%BB%8F%E9%AA%8C%E7%9A%84%E5%B7%A5%E5%86%9C%E5%85%B5%E5%AD%A6%E5%91%98%E2%80%9D%E6%88%90%E4%B8%BA%E5%8C%97%E4%BA%AC%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6%E7%9A%84%E5%AD%A6%E7%94%9F%E3%80%82 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In January 1978, Bai graduated from Peking University Department of Chemistry with a major in [[catalysis]]. In October 1978, He was admitted to the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] Institute of Chemistry, where he received a [[Master of Science]] in structural chemistry in 1981 and a [[Doctor of Science]] in 1985.<ref name="scitech.people.com.cn" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=白春礼 |url=https://www.hkbu.edu.hk/zh_cn/about/honorary-doctorates-and-honorary-university-fellows/bai-chunli.html |access-date=2022-09-17 |website=www.hkbu.edu.hk |publisher=[[Hong Kong Baptist University]] |archive-date=20 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920170851/https://www.hkbu.edu.hk/zh_cn/about/honorary-doctorates-and-honorary-university-fellows/bai-chunli.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=白春礼----中国科学院 |url=https://www.cas.cn/zt/jzt/djzt/ddsqdzt/zkysqddbjj/200708/t20070814_2670084.shtml |access-date=2022-09-17 |website=www.cas.cn |archive-date=20 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920171838/https://www.cas.cn/zt/jzt/djzt/ddsqdzt/zkysqddbjj/200708/t20070814_2670084.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=《授予博士、硕士学位和培养研究生的学科、专业目录》(1997年颁布) - 中华人民共和国教育部政府门户网站 |url=http://www.moe.gov.cn/srcsite/A22/moe_833/200512/t20051223_88437.html |access-date=2022-09-17 |website=www.moe.gov.cn |archive-date=20 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920171230/http://www.moe.gov.cn/srcsite/A22/moe_833/200512/t20051223_88437.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Career ==
In January 1978, after graduating from the university, Bai Chunli was assigned to the Chinese Academy of Sciences' applied chemistry department, which was the beginning of his research career in the Chinese Academy of Sciences. From 1985 to 1987, he did [[postdoctoral research]] in the [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]]. In 1996, he was the Vice President of the Chinese Academy of Sciences; in 2011, he took over from Lu Yongxiang as sixth President of Chinese Academy of Sciences, succeeded by [[Hou Jianguo]] in December 2020.

{{As of|2014}} Bai is currently a part-time professor at Peking University, [[Tsinghua University]], [[University of Science and Technology of China]], [[Nankai University]], and the [[China University of Geosciences (Wuhan)|China University of Geosciences]], and a visiting professor at [[Liaoning Normal University]] and [[Nanjing Audit University]].

He is also editor-in-chief of the journal ''[[National Science Review]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/national-science-review-2053714X|title=National Science Review|website=global.oup.com}}</ref>

M. T. |last4 = Wang |first4 = C. |last5 = Bai |first5 = C. }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1021/ja994271p |title = Alkane-Assisted Adsorption and Assembly of Phthalocyanines and Porphyrins |journal = Journal of the American Chemical Society |volume = 122 |issue = 23 |page = 5550 |year = 2000 |last1 = Qiu |first1 = X. |last2 = Wang |first2 = C. |last3 = Zeng |first3 = Q. |last4 = Xu |first4 = B. |last5 = Yin |first5 = S. |last6 = Wang |first6 = H. |last7 = Xu |first7 = S. |last8 = Bai |first8 = C. |bibcode = 2000JAChS.122.5550Q }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1021/nl015540o |bibcode = 2001NanoL...1..323L |title = Tuning the Chain Helicity and Organizational Morphology of anl-Valine-Containing Polyacetylene by pH Change |journal = Nano Letters |volume = 1 |issue = 6 |page = 323 |year = 2001 |last1 = Li |first1 = B. K. |last6 = Xiao |first6 = X. |last7 = Bai |first7 = C. |last8 = Tang |first8 = B. Z. }}</ref> and scanning tunneling microscopy,<ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1021/ma0213091 |bibcode = 2003MaMol..36...77L |title = Synthesis and Hierarchical Structures of Amphiphilic Polyphenylacetylenes Carryingl-Valine Pendants |journal = Macromolecules |volume = 36 |page = 77 |year = 2003 |last1 = Li |first1 = B. S. |last2 = Cheuk |first2 = K. K. L. |last3 = Ling |first3 = L. |last4 = Chen |first4 = J. |last5 = Xiao |first5 = X. |last6 = Bai |first6 = C. |last7 = Tang |first7 = B. Z. |issue = 1 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1021/ac026182s |title = Specific Aptamer−Protein Interaction Studied by Atomic Force Microscopy |journal = Analytical Chemistry |volume = 75 |issue = 9 |year = 2003 |last1 = Jiang |first1 = Y. |last2 = Zhu |first2 = C. |last3 = Ling |first3 = L. |last4 = Wan |first4 = L. |last5 = Fang |first5 = X. |last6 = Bai |first6 = C. |pages = 2112–6 |pmid=12720349}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1093/nar/26.20.4785 |pmid = 9753751 |title = A convenient method of aligning large DNA molecules on bare mica surfaces for atomic force microscopy |journal = Nucleic Acids Research |volume = 26 |issue = 20 |year = 1998 |last1 = Li |first1 = J. |last2 = Bai |first2 = C. |last3 = Wang |first3 = C. |last4 = Zhu |first4 = C. |last5 = Lin |first5 = Z. |last6 = Li |first6 = Q. |last7 = Cao |first7 = E.|pages = 4785–4786 |pmc = 147909 }}</ref> where his work focuses on scanning probe microscopy techniques, and molecular nano-structure, as well as nanotechnology research.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://english.cas.cn/Administration/Adators/200908/t20090825_33929.shtml |title=Bai Chunli-Chinese Academy Of Sciences |publisher=English.cas.cn |date=2011-03-07 |access-date=2012-06-05 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130704081318/http://english.cas.cn/Administration/Adators/200908/t20090825_33929.shtml |archive-date=2013-07-04 }}</ref> He has published a large number of books in both Chinese and English. He was an alternate committee member of the 15th and the 16th CPC Central Committee, and the sixth Vice President of the China Association for Science and Technology.

Bai conducted research in areas such as polymer catalyst structure and property, organic compounds of crystal structure X-ray diffraction, molecular mechanics and conductive polymers of EXAFS, etc. He has been engaged in the study of scanning tunneling microscopy, which has been a significant field in [[nanotechnology]] (NT), since the mid-1980s. Many of his works, both in Chinese and English, have been published by Germany Springer Publish Company and Scientific Company and many other publishing houses. Furthermore, he has earned many other awards such as Internationalism{{clarify|date=July 2012}} which is awarded by the International Chemical Industry association.

Bai Chunli is one of the pioneers in the field of [[scanning probe microscopy]]. The laboratory he leads organized much wide-ranging and detailed research. Bai has made many contributions to STM study nationally and internationally. He has created a team which aims to increase cooperation between China and the United States on the issue of regularly using energy sources. Bai has also devoted himself to shortening the scientific distance between China and foreign countries.

He is the editor of ''China Basic Science'' magazine, and plays an important role in the political field. In his youth, he was named the best worker around China and one of China's Top Ten Outstanding Young Persons among other distinctions.

His research has been published widely in [[peer review]]ed journals and books.<ref>{{cite web |url = http://www.spm.com.cn/chunli_bai.shtml |title = 白春礼院士著作 |publisher = Spm.com.cn |access-date = 2012-06-05 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131122053859/http://www.spm.com.cn/chunli_bai.shtml |archive-date = 2013-11-22 |url-status = dead }}</ref>

* Corresponding [[list of Fellows of the Australian Academy of Science|Member of the Australian Academy of Science]] in 2013<ref>{{Cite web |title=President of the Chinese Academy of Sciences admitted to the Academy {{!}} Australian Academy of Science |url=https://www.science.org.au/academy-newsletter/australian-academy-science-newsletter-99/president-chinese-academy-sciences |access-date=2022-04-21 |website=Australian Academy of Science |language=en |archive-date=2 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220902195501/https://www.science.org.au/academy-newsletter/australian-academy-science-newsletter-99/president-chinese-academy-sciences |url-status=live }}</ref>
* Laureate of the [[Asian Scientist 100]], ''[[Asian Scientist]]'', 2016 and 2022
* Honorary Member of Chinese Association for Science and Technology in 2011
* [[Fellow of the Royal Society|Foreign Member of the Royal Society (ForMemRS)]] in 2014<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chunli Bai |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/chunli-bai-11023/ |access-date=2022-04-21 |website=Royal Society |archive-date=26 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151126125507/https://royalsociety.org/people/chunli-bai-11023/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

* Honorary President of the [[University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences|University of Chinese Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="University of Science and Technology of China" />

His nomination for the Royal Society reads: {{centered pull quote|Dr. Chunli Bai is one of the pioneers in the field of nanoscience. In the mid-1980s, he successfully designed and developed China's first [[atomic force microscope|atomic force microscope (AFM)]], [[Scanning tunneling microscope|scanning tunneling microscope (STM)]], low-temperature STM, ultrahigh vacuum-STM, and [[Ballistic electron emission microscopy|ballistic electron emission microscope]]. These led to the earliest technological tools in the country for manipulating single atoms and molecules, and characterizing surfaces and interfaces. He successfully established a methodology for the study of molecular assembly on solid substrate surfaces, such as the imaging of functional molecules on [[graphite]] surfaces. His use of alkane-assisted adsorption and assembly in this context is particularly noteworthy. Beyond his outstanding scientific achievements, Dr. Bai's leadership role in Chinese science includes service as the President of the [[Chinese Chemical Society (Beijing)|Chinese Chemical Society]] (1998–2010), and Vice-President (1996–2004), Executive Vice-President (2004–2011) and President (2011–present) of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS). In 2012 he became the first Chinese President of the [[TWAS|Academy of Sciences for the Developing World (TWAS)]].<ref name="royal">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/fellowship/2014/chunli-bai/ |title=Professor Chunli Bai ForMemRS |publisher=The Royal Society |location=London |archive-date=2014-12-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141220122746/https://royalsociety.org/people/fellowship/2014/chunli-bai/ |url-status=live }}</ref>}}
